<!-- pr-reviewer: 8977cd5f09b8b2fbcec2cdf042936596038b24ed -->

Needs changes before merge.

What looks good:
- Written new, self-contained, small: the ring and row planners are new code with no old planner ported; `camcraft-pathkernel` still depends on `camcraft-geometry` only. `Guides` routes each family to its planner and refuses the medial line and the trace by name (law 4).
- Law-1 is pinned properly: 11 ring tests (level-set spacing, any pick order, Part == Boundary without a stock edge, the waist, clean-up fill, `FILL_MIN`, no clean-up on a count, open rings at the stock edge, each refusal) and 6 row tests (spacing, angle, closing ring, law 1, mark checks), all against the public API. The waist test pins the #3788 full-width stretch, with the two mouths getting clean-up rings.
- Marks are geometry (a canonical index plus the stretch points), `GuideSet::with_marks` renumbers and refuses a stray mark by name, and the canonical sort keeps the mark with its curve.
- The pins against the old rings (dog bone, 2D Pocket band, level rings) have the named differences written down (the stock-outline pass, #3316/#3750, the blind golden). The docs/decisions entry records the drop of the fixed `RING = 4` fill depth and of `full_width_at`, with the reason.
- Named refusals throughout, no unwrap/panic outside tests, provenance lines on all new modules, and the laws gate map includes all new modules.

Results (merged with the trial base `origin/side/path-kernel` at 6fb3d55ce - the merge is "Already up to date"; built locally in a review worktree, not the runner - base is a side branch, not main):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` (base 6fb3d55ce): green. pathkernel lib: 3 passed; pathkernel laws: 89 passed; motion pass_start_levels: 39 passed (incl. kernel_rings 2 and kernel_baseline 15).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Light lane: NOT run locally - three attempts were cut off by the 10-minute cap in the release build of the motion+app test binaries (still compiling the app's release test suite at the cap). The PR body names a green light run (6 of 6 steps) on the head before the side-branch merge, on the same code. A re-run at the cut gate covers the merged head; treating this as a note, not a blocker.
- Example catalog suites: not owed - no post or toolpath changed and no old planner calls the new code (the pins are the motion pass_start_levels suite, which ran). The body names green catalog runs on the head before the side-branch merge.

Targeted tests (step 5): no post or toolpath change, so no example_catalog suites owed. P2 issue (#4176), so no targeted heavy step. The light lane is the one step that did not run here (see above); not a pass.

Requested before merge:
1. The ring planner's completeness-guard target is narrowed when `first_offset > tool radius`, so the strip of the cutter-centre area within `first_offset - radius` of the wall is never cut and never named - the verdict reads `Done` for an uncut area. `crates/pathkernel/src/guide/rings.rs` (the `if d0 > rad { ... } else { p.center().clone() }` line in `plan`) hides that strip from the fill guard. Reproduce: a disc pocket, tool radius 3, first offset 5, stepover 2 - a scratch test through the public API gives a `Done` verdict with 6 curves and about 201 mm2 of the 17 mm-radius centre left uncut (the strip is exactly `pi * (17^2 - 15^2)` mm2, as expected). Fix by refusing the choice by name (e.g. `NO_RING`-style, or a named "first offset leaves the wall strip uncut") or by targeting the whole centre area and letting the guard/fill name the gap.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
- `GuideSet::with_marks` silently drops a mark whose curve was refused by the curve checks (the note names the curve, but the mark is lost silently - one-class-of-finder would close the class).
- The closing ring of a rows choice adds one raw per loop, so the hole boundary of an island gets a closing ring too. Probably intended (the closing ring the boundary of the area), but unpinned.
- A `FullWidth` mark on an open ring piece (`RingRef::Part`) uses the clip-kept stretches untested; the waist pins the closed case only.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: e872c5699d44c93878968fa386fd6c998fcb9221 -->

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good:
- The earlier blocking findings are fixed and pinned on this head. The completeness guard is one function (`cover::judge`) for both planners. It reads the region's own centre area and the finished set. A clearing ring choice with a first offset above the tool radius is refused by name (`WALL_STRIP_UNCUT`); a ring count names the uncut area in a note; the 0.1 mm2 limit is checked independently by the guard grids (`guide_guard.rs`, 8 tests).
- A refused curve names every mark that is not kept (`a_refused_curve_names_its_marks_in_its_note`). Each loop of the area gets a closing ring (`the_closing_ring_of_rows_runs_round_each_island_too`). A full-width stretch on an open ring round a part is named and pinned (`a_full_width_stretch_on_an_open_ring_round_a_part_is_named`).
- The planners are new, self-contained and small; `camcraft-pathkernel` still depends on `camcraft-geometry` only, and no geometry function was added. `Guides` refuses the medial line and the trace by name (law 4). Each new module has a provenance line; files stay under 400 lines; no registry row is added yet, documented in the body.
- Law 1 is pinned (any pick order, purity) and the pins against the recorded old rings (dog bone 29 rings, band 2D Pocket and 3-D level rings, both ways) carry the named differences with reasons.

Results (merged with the trial base `origin/side/path-kernel` at cb93488c0 - trial merge clean, "Already up to date"; built locally in a review worktree on the head `e872c5699d44`, not the runner - the base is a side branch, not main):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: green. pathkernel lib: 4 passed; pathkernel laws: 114 passed (incl. the guard grids); motion pass_start_levels: 39 passed (incl. kernel_rings 2 and kernel_baseline 15). Missing from the body's "final head" claim: the body names 89/17 on 74766eaa5; this head merged K5 (entry and exit) on top of that and adds 25 law-suite tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No example-catalog suites are owed: this PR changes no post and no toolpath, and no old planner calls the new code.
- Light lane: NOT run locally - the release build of the motion and app test binaries does not fit the review budget in this worktree (the same limit the previous review met). The author's green run names 7 of 7 steps on the pre-merge head 74766eaa5. The same code plus a merge is on this head. A re-run at the cut gate covers it; treating this as a note, not a blocker.

Targeted tests (step 5): no example-catalog suites (no post or toolpath change). P2, so no targeted heavy step. Light lane not run locally, noted above.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
- The body's gate claims name 74766eaa5; the head is now e872c5699d44 (a merge of the side branch). The quick gate named in the body (green on 74766eaa5) is re-verified here on e872c5699 locally: green.
- The law suite has no registry row yet for the two planners (the body documents that the row comes with the 2D Pocket migration). The pins named in the issue (L1, L2, L3, L4) all run in `tests/laws/` and pass; nothing waits on the registry row for this sub-PR.
- One doc-comment hunk of the `laws.rs` Gate map was hand-resolved in the merge of the side branch (the DELTA class). The resolution keeps both sides' module names and drops one duplicate entry; no logic changed. Confirmed by the diff against the base.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
